name: Winemaking: Vinification

outcome.intro: After studying this section, a student will understand the definition of winemaking (vinification), the steps of making white, red, and rosé, and other important factors of consideration that influence the how and why wines taste the way they do.
outcome.certified: After studying this section, a candidate will have a deeper understanding of winemaking cause and effect on the final wine aromas and flavors, such as fermentation techniques, barrel size choices, types of oak used, and other important winemaking decisions.

rows.intro: Vinification: Decisions and practices made in the winery from harvest to when the wine is bottled.
rows.certified: Basic chemistry of wine and how it relates to cause and effect. Malolactic conversion, acids in wine, and sugars in wine.

rows.intro: What is the goal of the winery?; What style of wine will be produced?; What will the price point of the wine be?; Are there regional wine laws the winery must adhere to?; Sustainability.
rows.certified: Breakdown of how sustainability is implemented in the winery.

rows.intro: Harvest; Sort; Destem; White Wines: Crush, Press, Fermentation, Fining/Filtering, Bottling/Packaging.; Red Wines; Crush, Maceration, Fermentation (with skin contact), Pressing, Aging, Fining/Filtration, Bottling/Packaging, Bottle Aging.; Rosé Wines (simple version); Crush (red grape varieties), Maceration skin contact (for a short time), Pressing, Fermentation, Fining/Filtration, Bottling/Packaging.
rows.certified: Three types of Rosé production: Maceration time; Blending Method - often used for sparkling wine production.; Saignée*; *Saignée or “bleeding” method (this essentially doesn't exist anymore. It was a concentration technique for red wine production with rosé being the byproduct.); Aging: Can be on the lees or without.; Can be in concrete, stainless steel, or oak.

rows.intro: Sugar + Yeast --> Alcohol, CO2, Heat, Aromas, Flavors
rows.certified: Saccharomyces cerevisiae = species of yeast for wine fermentation

rows.intro: Type of vessel; Wood; Stainless steel; Concrete
rows.certified: Exploration of oak and its various origins.; Identification of other types of woods used for barrels, such as acacia, cherry, and chestnut.; Barrel Sizes: Barrique = 225 liters; Puncheon = 300 liters; Demi-muid = 600 liters; Foudre/Botti = 1,000+ liters; Understand the cause and effect of the different types of vessels and which has more flavor impact. Know which major areas of the world use them, such as botti in Piemonte or barriques in Rioja.

rows.intro: Size: Large or small.; Shape: Oval, round, egg.; Oxygen permeability considerations.; Temperature control.
rows.certified: Basic knowledge of coopers and the construction of barrels.

rows.intro: Grape must; Chaptalization; Acidification; Water addition; Lees; Autolysis; Malolactic fermentation; Carbonic maceration
rows.certified: Cause & effect: Skin contact and its effect on color, extraction, pH, and texture.; Bâttonage and its effect on weight, flavor, and texture.; Whole-cluster versus stem inclusion versus whole-berry fermentations.; Be able to associate winemaking practices to a non-fruit descriptor on the Certified Exam Tasting Grid. Know which regions and grape varieties are associated with them and which are not: lees/autolysis, malolactic fermentation, carbonic maceration.

rows.intro: Temperature control and why it's important for different color wines and styles.; Oxygen management and its impact of final style of wine produced.; Extraction explained through the use of punch downs, pump overs, maceration times, and fermentation temperature.
rows.certified: Outlining the differences between reductive and oxidative winemaking.

rows.intro: Costs; Age of barrels; Length of time of aging
rows.certified: What each region dictates and what options winemakers have.

rows.intro: Clarification and the difference between fining and filtration.
rows.certified: Cold stabilization; Examples of fining agents; Sulphur additions and the difference between free and bound compounds.

rows.intro: Containers: Bottles; Kegs; Boxed wine; Closures: Cork; Composites; Screw cap (Stelvin); Glass top (Vinolok); Packaging: Labels and label design; Capsule colors and design; Adhering to governmental label laws
